rationale: The assistant correctly linked Er03 to the boil-over onto the controls, told the customer to isolate and dry it, and gave a sensible stop-use/engineer boundary if the code returned when dry or if there was a burning smell. It wrongly stated Er03 'is not a standard global error' (AEG documents it as liquid/object on the controls) and framed it as 'short circuits' and 'liquid tracking under the glass' rather than the simple sensor cut-off, with an overly cautious 24-hour wait that it then reasonably walked back. It asked no checks (e.g. anything resting on the control area, whether all zones work), but the outcome matched the ground truth with no part or escalation.
